_problem: 0022 (merged at 34429fc) shipped a complete, granted, audited job lifecycle that NOTHING calls. Verified on main: apps/bot/src/queues.ts is `[]`, worker.ts calls boss.start() then idles with no boss.work(), and claim_outbox_batch has zero TypeScript call sites. Four functions are GRANT EXECUTEd to app_worker at 0022:527-530 and have never been exercised from the runtime seat. Separately, DD-90 Q6 recorded that the provision-before-worker ordering has no runtime fence at all: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES in provision-queue.ts:39-45 only applies to objects created by the role that ran it, so any queue added without re-provisioning leaves app_worker without grants — and because QUEUES has always been empty, that path has never run with a real queue. AMENDED 2026-07-27 after slice 2a merged at 76e1f7b: 0023 discharged the ack requirement 0022:166-181 wrote against this slice, so the migration half is done and this slice is now correctly TypeScript-only. But 2a did not merely add a function — it changed claim_outbox_batch's RETURNS TABLE to six columns (event_id, tenant_id, aggregate_id, sequence, type, claim_token), and it made acking a per-event OBLIGATION of the dispatcher rather than an optional tidy-up. Without the ack call this handler reproduces exactly the starvation loop 2a exists to close: every event it processes successfully still expires its lease, gets reclaimed forever, and starves newer events. The ack is therefore a correctness requirement of THIS slice, not a nicety.
_decision_contract: DD-90 Q6 (owner-final 2026-07-25) is the hard contract of THIS slice and is not re-opened: a preflight runs BEFORE boss.start() — not before boss.work(), because startup itself already touches the pgboss schema — connecting as app_worker, asserting the pgboss schema and base objects, every queue in the registry, and the exact catalog grants plus sequence usage; any missing item exits non-zero before scheduler or maintenance runs. Tests must prove both directions: provision-first passes, and a missing queue or missing grant fails. DD-89 Q1 also binds: app_worker gets zero direct DML on projector_deliveries — every state transition goes through the four granted SECURITY DEFINER functions. TDD §3.4 binds the handler: claim_outbox_batch is a privileged cross-tenant call returning rows for many tenants, so before touching ANY tenant-scoped business data the handler must re-enter tenant context per row via the withTenant `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` choke-point — never a raw query. ADDED 2026-07-27 (0023, merged 76e1f7b): the handler MUST call ack_outbox_event(event_id, required_projectors, claim_token) once fan-out for an event is complete, and MUST pass the claim_token returned by that same claim_outbox_batch call — 0023 rejects a stale token as a no-op returning false, which is the guard against a zombie worker acking an event a live claimant is mid-flight on. It MUST pass the FULL list of required projectors: 0023 raises rather than acking if any named projector lacks a projector_deliveries row, deliberately turning 'caller forgot fan-out' into an exception instead of a silent premature ack. A false return is NOT success and must not be swallowed — it means the token was stale and another claimant owns the event.
_scope_in: One module, apps/bot. (1) NEW apps/bot/src/preflight.ts implementing the DD-90 Q6 assertions against an app_worker connection, exported as a pure function returning a structured result plus a fail-closed wrapper. (2) worker.ts calls it and exits non-zero BEFORE createQueue/boss.start() on any failure. (3) queues.ts registers the first real queue name. (4) NEW apps/bot/src/dispatcher.ts: one boss.work() handler running the full lifecycle already shipped in 0022 — claim_outbox_batch(limit) -> per event job_prepare_projector_delivery(event_id, projector) -> claim_projector_delivery_batch(projector, limit) -> complete_projector_delivery(event_id, projector, claim_token, result, next_attempt_at, provider_ref, error_code) for all three results delivered | retry | dlq. The step that would perform real projection work is behind an INJECTED interface; this slice ships no production implementation of it. (5) Tests for both files, including a real app_worker seat. (6) The ack step: after fan-out for an event completes, call ack_outbox_event with that event's claim_token and the full required-projector list; handle the false return (stale token — another claimant owns it, do not retry the ack) distinctly from the raise (fan-out incomplete — a bug in this handler, fail loudly). (7) The required-projector registry as a code-owned constant, since 0023 made the list a runtime argument and it does not exist anywhere yet.
_scope_out: NO PRODUCER — owner-decided 2026-07-26, DEFERRED_OUT_OF_SCOPE. This slice must not add any INSERT into outbox_events outside test fixtures, and must not treat 'the loop runs with a test enqueue' as evidence that it runs with real business data. Choosing whether producers live in sync-engine or per-feature is explicitly NOT answered here. NO cron/schedule registration (slice 3). NO real projector implementation or surface_refs access (slice 4 and the first concrete projector own those; the delivery step stays injected with no production impl). NO edit to provision-queue.ts, queue.ts options, or any 0000-0023 migration — the DDL/grant authority boundary from DD-89 Q2 stays exactly where it is. NO new migration — this is now a HARD boundary rather than an oversight: slice 2a (0023, merged 76e1f7b) discharged the schema half, so any migration appearing in this slice means its scope has drifted back into 2a's territory and it HALTs. NO RLS policy or GRANT change. NO change to claim ordering (ORDER BY created_at is the sync-engine contract per DD-89 Q3). NO direct DML on outbox_events, projector_deliveries or job_audit_events from app_worker.
_design_probe: Required per canonical autopilot-prompt-GENERIC v0.6.1 §0.1 — this slice hits trigger (2) choke-point mutating projector_deliveries state, (6) amends merged core (the 0022 functions and the boss.start() path), and (8) new mechanism choice. Before any production edit, write .autopilot/state/job-runtime-dispatcher/design-probe.md pinning FOUR things and STOP for founder confirm: (a) the exact preflight assertion list and how each is queried from the app_worker seat — schema presence, per-queue presence, and the exact catalog privilege rows, since 'assert grants' is not self-executing; (b) the queue name and the projector identifier, both code-owned constants; (c) the retry policy — what next_attempt_at the handler supplies on 'retry', what turns a retry into 'dlq', and where that bound lives, given 0022 stores attempts but deliberately leaves policy to the consumer; (d) the shape of the injected delivery interface and how tests exercise delivered/retry/dlq without a real projector. A mechanical mirror of slice 1 would get (c) and (d) wrong. ADDED after 0023 merged (2026-07-27), item (e), and it is now the item a mechanical mirror is most likely to get wrong: ack_outbox_event takes p_required_projectors text[] and RAISES if any named projector lacks a delivery row, so this slice must decide WHERE that list lives and what it contains. The convenient answer — pass the single projector this slice happens to register — is indistinguishable from correct today and reintroduces exactly the failure 0023's array argument exists to prevent, one layer up: a second projector registered later would be silently omitted from the list and the event would ack before it was delivered. Pin whether the list is derived from the same constant that drives fan-out (so the two cannot diverge by construction) or is a second independent constant (so they can), and justify. Also pin how the false return of ack_outbox_event is distinguished from the raise in the handler's control flow, because the two mean opposite things: false is 'another claimant owns this, do nothing', raise is 'this handler has a bug'.
_acceptance: JRD-1: preflight passes on a cluster where provision-queue ran AFTER the queue was registered; process proceeds to boss.start().
JRD-2: preflight FAILS non-zero when a queue in the registry has no pgboss partition — the exact DD-90 Q6 provision-ordering fence.
JRD-3: preflight FAILS non-zero when app_worker is missing any asserted grant or sequence usage on the pgboss schema, even though the queue exists.
JRD-4: preflight runs BEFORE boss.start() — a test proves no pg-boss startup or maintenance work happened when preflight fails (not merely that the process exited).

JRD-5: NEGATIVE ASSERTION — REWRITTEN 2026-07-27. The original wording ('every tenant-scoped read goes through withTenant') was vacuous: the AP-33 design probe established that this handler reads NO tenant-scoped business data at all. claim_outbox_batch is a privileged cross-tenant read returning tenant_id as data, and job_prepare_projector_delivery derives tenant_id internally from the event row at 0022:298 rather than from the caller's session, so a withTenant test would pass by having nothing to exercise. Assert the invariant structurally instead: the shipped handler issues ZERO SQL outside the five granted SECURITY DEFINER function calls, and references no table other than outbox_events, projector_deliveries and job_audit_events. Record explicitly that TDD §3.4's withTenant choke-point becomes binding the moment the injected delivery interface gains a production implementation that reads tenant data — that is slice 4's obligation, and it must not inherit this slice's negative assertion as though the question were already settled.
JRD-6: prepare is idempotent — the same (event_id, projector) prepared twice yields one delivery row.
JRD-7: delivered path — claim returns a token, complete with the exact token transitions to delivered, attempts increments once, token/lease cleared.
JRD-8: retry path — complete with 'retry' and a strictly future next_attempt_at moves to failed; the row is re-claimable only once due; the stale token cannot complete after re-claim.
JRD-9: dlq path — terminal; no further claim or completion succeeds.
JRD-10: expired lease is reclaimed on the next claim, and job_audit_events shows more than one row for that job_id (0022 deliberately has no UNIQUE(job_id)).
JRD-11: app_worker still has ZERO direct DML on outbox_events, projector_deliveries and job_audit_events — the handler path uses only the four granted functions.
JRD-12: no INSERT into outbox_events exists in shipped code — grep the diff; only test fixtures may seed events.
JRD-13: worker still starts with migrate:false and DATABASE_URL_DIRECT required; no DDL is attempted from the runtime seat.
JRD-14: full workspace suite green and the migration tail is unchanged at 0023 — this slice adds no migration, and the db suite count is unchanged at 212 because every test it adds lives in apps/bot.

JRD-15: ACK CLOSES THE LOOP — the row this amendment exists for. Process an event end-to-end through the handler, advance past the five-minute lease, call claim_outbox_batch again, and assert the event is NOT returned. Without the ack call this fails and reproduces the starvation loop 0023 was written to close.

JRD-16: STALE-TOKEN PATH — force a second claimant to reclaim an event mid-flight, then let the first handler attempt its ack; assert ack_outbox_event returns false, the handler treats it as 'another claimant owns this' without retrying or raising, and acked_at stays NULL.

JRD-17: FAN-OUT COMPLETENESS IS EXERCISED, NOT ASSUMED — register a second projector in the required list, deliberately skip preparing its delivery, and assert ack_outbox_event RAISES and the handler surfaces it as a defect rather than swallowing it. A green run with only one projector registered does not satisfy this row.
_scope_exception: Budget: this P1 runtime slice spans one module (apps/bot) but ~5 files including two new source files and two new test files, above the nominal 3-file comfort. Splitting preflight from the handler was considered and rejected: DD-90 Q6 says the preflight exists to fence the first real queue registration, so a preflight slice with QUEUES still empty would assert nothing and prove nothing — the two land together or neither is verifiable. No migration is added, so the single-monotonic-migration budget is untouched — the schema half is slice 2a (0023, merged 76e1f7b).
_evidence_rules: Re-verify on synced main before coding: claim_outbox_batch's RETURNS TABLE must have SIX columns including claim_token (0023 changed it from five — if it still has five, 0023 has been reverted and the premise is gone), ack_outbox_event's exact three-argument signature and its GRANT EXECUTE to app_worker, the other four 0022 function signatures and their GRANT lines (they are the contract, not this manifest's prose), QUEUES still empty, worker.ts still lacking boss.work(), and provision-queue.ts unchanged. Read 0022:166-181 and confirm it now points at a discharged requirement. If any differ, HALT DESIGN_UNFIT rather than adapting silently. Do not invent a retry/backoff policy, or a required-projector list, in code before it is pinned in the design probe and confirmed.
